title: GitOps & Progressive Delivery (Argo CD, Flux & Rollouts)
summary: Implement OpenGitOps principles with Argo CD and Flux: pull-based reconciliation, automated drift healing, and progressive Canary/Blue-Green delivery.
learningObjectives: Apply the four OpenGitOps principles (Declarative, Versioned/Immutable, Pulled Automatically, Continuously Reconciled).
Synchronize OutOfSync Argo CD Applications and verify self-healing workload reconciliation.
Configure Argo Rollouts for progressive Canary traffic delivery.

curriculumModules.title: Pull-Based GitOps Reconciliation with Argo CD
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Instead of CI pipelines pushing `kubectl apply` with cluster-admin tokens, an in-cluster GitOps agent (Argo CD) pulls desired state from Git and continuously heals configuration drift.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Use the App-of-Apps or `ApplicationSet` pattern to manage multi-cluster fleets from an immutable Git repository with branch protection and signed commits.

curriculumModules.title: Progressive Delivery: Canary & Blue-Green Rollouts
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Argo Rollouts replaces standard Deployments with a `Rollout` controller that shifts traffic incrementally (`10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%`) while querying Prometheus SLO metrics.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Pair Argo Rollouts with an AnalysisTemplate that automatically aborts and rolls back a canary release if HTTP 5xx exceeds 1% or P99 latency exceeds 250ms.

labs.title: Synchronizing OutOfSync Production Fleet with Argo CD
labs.scenario: A new Git commit updated the `checkout-gitops` application in Argo CD, leaving it `OutOfSync`. Synchronize the application and verify its pods are running in `production`.
labs.productionContext: GitOps operators monitor sync status and trigger or automate reconciliation to guarantee cluster state matches Git.
objectives: Inspect Argo CD applications using `argocd app list`
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: checkout-gitops
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  source:
    repoURL: https://github.com/kubelabs-io/gitops-fleet
    targetRevision: main
    path: apps/checkout
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: production

steps.title: Check Argo CD Sync Status
steps.instruction: Run `argocd app list` to see `checkout-gitops` in `OutOfSync` status.

validationRules.description: Argo CD Application checkout-gitops is Synced & Healthy
validationRules.name: checkout-gitops
checkout-gitops
validationRules.remediation: Verify checkout-gitops pods are Running in production after sync.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Run `argocd app get checkout-gitops` to confirm `Sync Status: Synced` and `Health Status: Healthy`.

labs.title: Deploying a Progressive Canary Rollout Workload
labs.scenario: Deploy an Argo `Rollout` resource named `search-canary` in `production` with 3 replicas for progressive canary delivery.
labs.productionContext: Progressive delivery limits blast radius by exposing new versions to a small percentage of users before full promotion.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: search-canary
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: search-canary
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: search-canary
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: search
          image: ghcr.io/kubelabs/search:v2.1.0
labs.troubleshootingGuide: Check `kubectl get rollout search-canary -n production` to verify `3/3` replicas are ready.

assessmentQuestions.question: Why is pull-based GitOps (Argo CD / Flux) more secure than traditional push-based CI/CD pipelines?
options: It stores cluster-admin credentials in public GitHub repositories
External CI runners never need direct network access or cluster-admin credentials to the production Kubernetes API server
It disables TLS verification on kube-apiserver
It allows developers to SSH directly into worker nodes
assessmentQuestions.explanation: In pull-based GitOps, the reconciliation controller runs inside the cluster and pulls desired state from Git, keeping production cluster credentials off external CI servers.

assessmentQuestions.question: What happens when `selfHeal: true` is enabled on an Argo CD automated sync policy and someone manually edits a Deployment via `kubectl edit`?
options: Argo CD commits the manual change back to the main branch in Git
Argo CD detects the live cluster drift against Git and automatically overwrites the manual change to restore the Git state
Argo CD deletes the entire namespace
assessmentQuestions.explanation: With `selfHeal: true`, Git remains the single source of truth; any out-of-band manual change is automatically reverted to match the Git revision.
